The test results for CBC, CRP, and ESR will inform our next steps, but your mention of fever and skin lesions alongside wrist pain is concerning. Can you describe the appearance of these skin lesions and tell me if the wrist pain is worse with movement?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE_BLOOD_COUNT: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; CRP: NORMAL READINGS; ESR: NORMAL READINGS; Skin_lesions: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm; Wrist_X-Ray: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (EN). The combination of fever, elevated WBC, and pathognomonic "lepromatous nodules" (violaceous vesiculopustular lesions) on the wrists and palms confirms this diagnosis, despite normal inflammatory markers and a normal X-ray ruling out septic arthritis or osteomyelitis.
